record.original_question: A Gδ set is a subset of a topological space that is a countable intersection of open sets. Let E be a Gδ set of measure zero on |z| = 1. Then does there exist an f in H ∞ , f 6= 0 such that f = 0 on E, and every point of the unit circle is a Fatou point of f ? (L. A. Rubel)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc, and let $\mathbb{T}=\{z:|z|=1\}$ be its boundary. Denote by $H^\infty=H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ the Banach space of bounded holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{D}$. A point $\zeta\in\mathbb{T}$ is called a Fatou point of $f\in H^\infty$ if the radial limit
$$f^*(\zeta)=\lim_{r\to 1^-}f(r\zeta)$$
exists (as a finite complex number). A subset of a topological space is called a $G_\delta$ set if it can be written as a countable intersection of open sets, and "measure zero" on $\mathbb{T}$ refers to one-dimensional Lebesgue (arc-length) measure.

Question: Let $E\subset\mathbb{T}$ be a $G_\delta$ set of Lebesgue measure zero. Does there exist a function $f\in H^\infty$, not identically zero, such that:
(i) every point of $\mathbb{T}$ is a Fatou point of $f$, and
(ii) the boundary radial-limit function $f^*$ satisfies $f^*(\zeta)=0$ for every $\zeta\in E$?
artifact.category_tag: Boundary behavior of bounded analytic functions
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related results on radial-limit failure sets (Lohwater–Piranian for $F_\sigma$ measure-zero sets, Kolesnikov's $G_{\delta\sigma}$ result, and recent work on boundary behavior of bounded analytic functions), but no source clearly resolves Rubel's specific question about producing a nonzero $H^\infty$ function whose radial limits exist everywhere on $\mathbb{T}$ and vanish on a prescribed $G_\delta$ measure-zero set. Status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: On the boundary behavior of bounded analytic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper on boundary radial-limit behavior of H^∞ functions, citing Kolesnikov and related characterizations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies which boundary sets can be exceptional sets for radial limits of H^∞ functions, but does not appear to settle Rubel's problem directly.

status_evidence.title: On sets of nonexistence of radial limits of bounded analytic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses characterization of F_σ and G_δσ measure-zero sets as exceptional sets for radial limits.
status_evidence.claim: Related characterizations exist, but the specific Rubel question about Fatou points everywhere with prescribed Gδ zero set is not clearly resolved in cited literature.
